The first piece of the word, the same strings standing as whole tokens ('ad', 'on'), and words GPT-2 keeps in a single token stay near zero however rare ('consonants', 'Mediterranean', 'Gettysburg', 'Rembrandt'), and the size of the peak follows the fragment pair rather than the meaning, so an invented word with the same split fires identically ('Paladina' = 'Paladino' = 2.03); a weaker, inconsistent minority of peaks instead falls on whole formal benefactive verbs and adjectives ('liable', 'owed', 'grateful', 'donated', 'provided') where a plainer synonym fires less.

Press release

The county archive will reopen to the public next month after a closure that lasted more than a year, and staff say they expect a steady flow of visitors through the autumn. The building was shut in the spring of last year, when water came through the roof and forced the county to move its collection into the basement of the old school on the far side of town. Volunteers spent the summer sorting boxes, labelling folders, and checking the shelf list against the catalogue. Much of the work was slow and dull. Several volunteers said they would not have stayed had the room been colder or the hours longer, and the county has since agreed to pay for hot drinks and bus fares.

The collection itself reaches back to the founding of the town. It includes land deeds, tax rolls, court minutes, parish registers, school log books, and a long run of local newspapers on microfilm. The oldest item is a leather ledger that records the sale of cattle at the market in the year of the great fire. Staff have now begun to photograph each page so that the originals can be kept away from the light. The museum will also show a small display of objects found in the roof space, among them a brass key, a set of clay pipes, a child's shoe, and a bundle of letters tied with string.

Opening hours will be Tuesday to Saturday, from ten in the morning until four in the afternoon, and staff ask that visitors book a seat in advance during the first month. Those who wish to consult original documents will be asked to leave bags and coats in a locker by the door and to use a pencil rather than a pen. Photography without flash will be allowed for private study, though a small fee will apply for commercial use. The friends of the archive have raised money for a new scanner, and a local trust has promised a grant to cover the cost of boxing the newspapers.

Curators say the display is meant to give visitors a sense of how ordinary people lived, rather than to celebrate the rich or the famous. Labels will be printed in plain language, and a free guide will be available at the desk. The reading room will hold twenty seats, two computers, and a small reference shelf with maps, directories, and indexes to the parish registers.

Anyone with documents, photographs, or recorded memories to add to the collection is asked to contact the office by post or by telephone. Staff will make a copy for the archive and return the original to the owner. The county said it hopes the archive will become a place where families can trace their own history, and where school groups can learn how the town grew. The new reading room is fitted with a state-of-the-art cataloguing system, and the first records should appear online before the end of the year.
